title: Arithmetic Progressions
seo_title: Arithmetic Progressions Class 10 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 5)
standard_text: Motivation for studying arithmetic progression; derivation of the nth term and sum of the first n terms of an AP and their application in solving daily life problems (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 10 Arithmetic Progressions worksheet (NCERT Chapter 5): common difference, nth term, finding a and d, sum of n terms and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How it works

An arithmetic progression (AP) is a list where each term is the previous term plus a fixed number d, the common difference.

nth term: an = a + (n − 1)d. Sum of the first n terms: Sn = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d] = n/2 (a + l), where l is the last term.

Example

Find the 10th term of 2, 7, 12, …

a = 2, d = 5

a10 = 2 + 9 × 5

Answer: 47

Example

Find the sum of the first 22 terms of 8, 3, −2, …

a = 8, d = −5

S = 11 [16 + 21 × (−5)]

Answer: −979

Common mistakes

  • Using a + nd for the nth term. It is a + (n − 1)d.
  • Finding d as a₁ − a₂. Always subtract a term from the next one: d = a₂ − a₁.
  • Forgetting to halve: S = n/2 (a + l), not n(a + l).

faq.q: What is the formula for the nth term of an AP?
faq.a: aₙ = a + (n − 1)d, where a is the first term and d is the common difference.

faq.q: What is the formula for the sum of the first n terms of an AP?
faq.a: Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d], or Sₙ = n/2 (a + l) when the last term l is known.

faq.q: How do I check whether a list is an AP?
faq.a: Find the differences between consecutive terms. If they are all equal, the list is an AP.

items.e: Middle term × 2 = sum of the outer terms: 2(2k + 5) = (1k + 3) + (6k − 8), so k = 5.
